newsitem.title: CHINA: Dismal dawn breaks over the new Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Dismal dawn breaks over the new Hong Kong.

text.p: As a dismal grey dawn broke over the new Hong Kong, two People's Liberation Army sentries stood impassively to attention outside the Prince of Wales Barracks.
Curious onlookers queued up in torrential rain to take each other's photograph with the soldiers now guarding Communist China's Special Administrative Region.

Their officer politely shooed away anyone who stepped over the entrance line to the barracks, named after the Prince of Wales who had sailed away from the dockside on the royal yacht Britannia only hours before.
The soldiers looked bemused by all the attention. The constant photo-taking ironically mirrored the scene outside Buckingham Palace where tourists love to snap the guardsmen.

Along the waterfront, officials raised China's five-starred red flag. But it hung limply in the rain, echoing the mood of a city nursing a giant hangover after the mammoth handover party of the night before.
The Star Ferry forlornly hooted its horn as it cut across the "Fragrant Harbour" in driving rain. The magnificent panorama of soaring skyscrapers had vanished from view.
Beside the ferry entrance, a relic of empire snoozed away the early hours of the morning. The 80-year-old rickshaw driver stretched out for a nap, too tired to tout for tourists.
In Statue Square, the Filipina maids enjoying one of their rare days off huddled under umbrellas and caught up on news.

It was business as usual for the newspaper vendors. Crouched in doorways, stripped to the waist in the cloying humidity, they stacked up the dailies heralding a new dawn for Hong Kong after 156 years of British colonial rule.
The refuse collectors in black plastic raincoats cleared mountains of rubbish left by the revellers.
But the constant downpour at dawn was enough to dampen the spirits of the most ardent partygoer.
Outside Joe Bananas bar in Wanchai, they stood out in the rain, lost in a haze of alcohol. Not a policeman was in sight.
The drunks were straggling their way home on automatic pilot, their feet splashing in the flooded streets of a city that never sleeps and now faces the dawn of an uncertain new era.
